newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel approves interim nuclear waste bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel approves interim nuclear waste bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Energy committee Thursday passed a bill to build a temporary storage facility in Nevada for radioactive waste from nuclear power plants.
President Clinton has threatened to veto the bill, which Nevada's two Democratic Senators oppose.

The committee passed the bill 15-5 after rejecting several amendments offered by New Mexico Democrat Jeff Bingaman to extend deadlines, limit the facility's capacity and increase environmental reviews of the proposed waste dump.

Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, said tight deadlines were necessary to prevent prolonged stalling on the project, which is to store nuclear waste until a permanent repository is built in about 15 years.

The Clinton administration opposes Murkowski's bill, saying it would designate Nevada as the nation's nuclear waste dump without a thorough review, and would divert resources from the permanent repository now under study to be built at Yucca Mountain in Nevada.

Bingaman said as the bill was written, if the administration decided not to go forward with the permanent repository in Yucca Mountain, "The defacto result is putting the waste on a cement pad in Nevada and then we're telling Nevada it's up to them to decide how to get ride of it."

But Murkowski said the government must have a way to dispose of the waste to avoid massive lawsuits from utilities, which have paid some $12 billion into a fund to be able to move the waste offsite starting next year, and to build a central repository.
The Senate passed Murkowski's bill last year, but with four fewer votes than the two-thirds majority needed to override Clinton's threatened veto.
Nevada's senators have said they still expect to have the votes to sustain a presidential veto.
The federal government is under legal obligation to start taking control of the nuclear waste, now in storage near nuclear reactors across the country, by January 31, 1998.
